summary: Public zygote time-lapse movies exist (mouse S-BIAD2356, ascidian S-BIAD1167 with CC BY 4.0, C. elegans S-BIAD1027, human IVF frames on Zenodo 15059361), but none provides pronuclear coordinate tracks, egg-centre positions or amphibian eggs; a test would have to segment both pronuclei and the egg outline from the raw movies, and the species are nematode, ascidian, mouse and human rather than the frog Thompson illustrated.
next_step: Pick one raw movie set with both pronuclei visible (S-BIAD2356 mouse, or the sea-urchin/ascidian literature), segment pronuclei and egg centre per frame, and pre-register the three geometric predictions (inside-triangle, convexity, pre-central meeting) on those tracks.
obstacles_confirmed: Ready-made coordinate tables are rarer than the movies.
Public movies are concentrated on nematode, mouse and echinoderm eggs rather than the frog geometry Thompson illustrated.
